paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples

model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the performance of two example selection methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—as a function of the number of in-context examples, measured by the metric minADE₂₀ (lower is better). The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," ranges from 0 to 15 in integer increments, with a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (↓)", ranges from 0.58 to 0.66, also on a linear scale, and indicates that lower values correspond to better performance. For the ST-ES method, the performance starts at 0.66 when no examples are provided, then drops sharply to 0.58 at 1 example, dips slightly to 0.57 at 3 examples, and then remains relatively stable around 0.57 to 0.58 for the remaining examples up to 15. In contrast, the Random method starts at 0.64 with 0 examples, decreases slightly to 0.63 at 1 example, and then remains nearly constant around 0.63 to 0.64 across the rest of the range. The plot shows that ST-ES achieves significantly better performance than Random, especially when only a few examples are used, and maintains a consistent advantage across all example counts.
